content:
This appendix, titled 'CONDUCT IN TEMPLE', outlines the proper code of conduct for devotees visiting a temple, based on excerpts from the Vaikhānasa texts, specifically Bhṛgu's Prakīrṇādhikāra (Chapters 20 and 36). The text emphasizes that these rules apply to both male and female devotees and are crucial for maintaining the temple's sacred atmosphere.

The appendix enumerates several prescriptions and prohibitions, organized into 27 points:

1.  **Entry**: One must not enter a shrine or its precincts in a vehicle or with footwear.
    (अपचाराः.........)
    यानैवो पादुकैवापि गमनं भगवद् गृहे ॥ (36,1)
2.  **Circumambulation (Pradakṣiṇā)**: Before entering, a devotee must circumambulate the shrine, keeping it to their right, in a deliberate and unhurried manner.
    प्रदक्षिणं शनैर्गत्वा देवालयमुपाव्रजेत्। (20, 113)
3.  **Respect for Temple Structure**: The temple and its towers are considered a form of the Godhead and must never be trodden upon.
    विमानं विष्णुरूपं स्यान्न तत्पदादिना क्रमेत्। (27,280)
4.  **Prostration**: One must prostrate or bow before the shrine before performing circumambulation.
    धामप्रदक्षिणे पूर्वं कुर्यात्तत्र नमस्क्रियाः । (ibid)
5.  **Shadows**: It is permissible to step on the shadow of the gopura, vimāna, prākāra, or dhvaja only during circumambulation, and not otherwise.
    न लंघयेद् ध्वजच्छायां प्रदक्षिणविधिं विना । गोपुरस्य विमानस्य प्राकारस्यालयस्य च॥ (27, 281)
6.  **Attire (Sacred Cord and Lower Garment)**: The sacred cord must be worn correctly, not apasavya or nivīta. The dhoti must be well tucked up (kaccha) without a hanging end (puccha). One must not enter naked or wearing only a loincloth (kaupīna).
    यज्ञसूत्रमधः कृत्वा कर्णे कृत्वा विशेषतः । अपसव्यं च धृत्वैव धृत्वा चैव विनीतवत्।। न गच्छेद्देवतागारं न वा मुक्ताशिखो नरः। अकच्छः पुच्छकच्छश्च कौपीनमात्रधृक् ॥ (36,312-313)
7.  **Attire (Upper Garment and Prohibitions)**: A neat upper cloth (uttarīya) must be worn. Stitched garments (shirts, coats), blankets, headgear (caps, turbans), and weapons are prohibited.
    यदा विशेद्गृहं विष्णोः सेवार्थं मधुविद्विषः। कृत्वोपवीतः सम्यगुत्तरीयं मनोहरम्। सेवेत देवदेवेशमुपवीतः सदा शुचिः ॥ कंचुकेनावृतांगस्तु न गच्छेद्धरि मन्दिरम्। उष्णीषी न च सेवेत नैव पाणौ धृतायुधः ॥ वस्त्रेणाच्छाद्य देहं तु कम्बलेनेतरेण वा॥ (36, 555-558)
8.  **Offerings and Consumption**: Do not enter empty-handed; bring an offering (flowers, fruits, etc.). Do not eat outside food or chew betel leaves inside. The forehead must bear a religious mark.
    रिक्तहस्तः शून्यफालस्त्यक्तसंव्यान एव च। खादन्नपि च ताम्बुलमुपहारादि भक्षयन्। देवालयं विशन्नैव तस्या पापं समुद्भवेत्॥ (36,314)
9.  **Prasāda**: It is improper to eat prasāda within the temple and leave leftovers on the premises.
    यो भुक्त्वा देवतागारे निक्षिप्योच्छिष्टमत्र तु । गच्छेदन्यत्र वा प्राऽस्यात् सोऽपि मूढो विपद्यते ॥ (36, 336)
10. **Health and Purity**: Those in physical or mental distress, or who are sick, should not enter. One must not evacuate bowels or expel flatulence inside.
    आर्ती प्रविशेद् गेहं देवस्य परमात्मनः । वायुभूते शरिरेऽस्मिन् वायुसंचारकर्मणि। मलवायुविसर्गस्तु देवगेहे विशेषतः ॥ पातयेत्पुरूषं सत्यमपि वेदान्तपारागम्। इति देवगृहं गन्तुं व्याधितो नैव चार्हति ।। (36, 548-552)
11. **Mental State**: Worship is only effective with a pure, steady, and calm mind.
    मनोऽनवस्थितं यस्य न साऽलं पूजितुं हरिम् । यस्यैव निर्मलं चित्तं सोऽर्हः सर्वेषु कर्मसु ।।
12. **Posture and Demeanor**: Do not stretch legs, sleep, or be inebriated. Be alert, humble, and erect.
    यस्तु देवगृहद्वारे प्रसार्य चरणौ क्वचित्। शेते निद्रातिसम्मोहात् स याति नरकायुतम्।। यातनाश्चानुभूयैव दौर्बाह्मण्यं व्रजेन्तु सः। यस्तु देवगृहे मूढः शयीत मदमोहितः ॥ (36, 337 and 340)
13. **Emotional Display**: Do not cry in anguish or weep, even in devotion, as grief is a mental blemish.
    यस्तु देवगृहं गत्वा रोदिति प्रणयाद्यथा । दुःखितः स्तौति वा देवं तत्स्यान्मानसिकं मलम्॥ निर्वाणपरमं स्थानं मलानेन मनसा तु यः। सेवते स न जानाति तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ॥ (36, 422-423)
14. **Purity of Being**: Worship requires a heart free from passion, speech free from falsehood and harshness, and a body abstaining from violence.
    रागाद्यपेतं हृदयं वागदुष्टाऽनृतादिना । हिंसादिरहितः कायः केशवाराधने त्रयम्॥ (36, 470)
15. **Non-Violence**: Never commit acts of violence. The six gateways to Dharma are listed as non-violence, virtuous conduct, meditation, sense control, penance, and service to elders.
    नैवात्र हिंसां कुर्वीत प्राणिनां दःखदां क्वचित्। अहिंसा वैदिकं कर्म ध्यानमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः । तपोऽथ गुरुशुश्रुषा धर्मद्वाराः षडीरिताः ॥ (36, 427)
16. **Speech**: Avoid gossip and needless chatter. The time should be used for meditation on God.
    मुधा संभाषते यस्तु प्रविष्य हरिमन्दिरम्। स निधि पुरतः सिद्धं त्यक्त्वा भिक्षति काकिणीम् ॥... तस्माद्देवगृहं गत्वा नरो नाऽन्यपरो भवेत् ॥ (36, 381-393 and 386-387)
17. **Truthfulness**: Never utter a lie in God's presence.
    न हि देवस्य पुरतः क्वचिदप्यनृतं वदेत्। सत्यस्वरूपी भगवान् सत्यं तस्मै न गृहयेत्।। (36,389)
18. **Intellectual Activities**: The temple is not for scriptural discussions, reading, writing, or argumentative talk.
    न हि देवगृहं गत्वा शास्त्राथैर्नीरसैर्नरः ।...स भवेदक्षरद्रोही यस्तु कृर्याद् व्यतिक्रमम्॥ (36,416, and 320)
19. **Quarrels**: Do not quarrel in a temple.
    न हि देवगृहं गत्वा विवदेत नरः क्वचित्। न तत् स्थानं विवादस्य तस्मात्तं दूरतस्त्यजेत्॥ (36,468)
20. **Humility**: Avoid self-eulogy and arrogance.
    आत्मानं यो विशेषेण स्तौत्यहंकार भावितः ।...अवलिप्तो न जानति दोषमात्मन्नि संगतम् ।। (36,600-601)
21. **Interaction with Others**: Do not speak contemptuously to others, talk ill of others, or praise another human being. God alone is praiseworthy.
    न जातु त्वमिति ब्रूयादापन्नो पि महत्तरं ।...त्यजेद्देवगृहे यस्तु सुखं मन्येत जीवितुम् ।। (36, 561, 564-5, 569-70)
22. **Greeting Others**: Do not greet or bow before another person in the temple, as all are subordinate to God.
    नैवान्यं प्रणमेज्जातु प्रविश्य हरिमन्दिरम्। स हि सर्वेश्वरः शेषी यत्राऽस्ते रमाधवः ॥ (36, 595)
23. **Facing the Deity**: Never sit with one's back to the Deity. Always face the Deity or keep it to the right.
    न हि देवगृहं गत्वा पृष्टीकृत्यासनं चरेत्।...पार्श्वतस्तु चरन्नेव निवर्तेतालयं प्रति ॥ (36, 593-594)
24. **Timing of Darśana**: Do not force a viewing of the Deity when the sanctum is screened or closed. Visit only at the appointed times.
    यस्त्वधीकारगर्वेण देवागारमुपाश्रितः ।...तस्मादकालसेवां तु विधिना परिवर्जयेत्।। (36, 627-633)
25. **Virtuous Conduct**: Only a virtuous person should undertake scriptural activities like visiting a temple.
    दुराचारो हि पुरुषो नेहायुर्विन्दते महत्।...तस्मादाचारवानेव कुर्याद्वै वैदिकाः क्रियाः ॥ (36,316)
26. **Proper Attitude**: Life is wasted without worship. Blameworthy attitudes include viewing the guru as merely human, the deity as stone, mantras as a livelihood, or being indifferent to rituals.
    विषयाक्रान्तचित्रानां विष्णवर्चनमकुर्वताम्।...जीवितं तस्य निष्फलम्।। (36, 633-636)
27. **Summary of Offences**: The appendix culminates with a consolidated list of twenty-two specific acts considered offensive in a temple, which are largely a summary of the preceding points.

The document concludes by advising that devotees should carefully avoid these offenses and should ask for forgiveness (kṣamā-yācanā) for any offenses committed inadvertently, as this counteracts their ill effects.
    अपचारास्तथा विष्णोर्द्वाविंशत् परिकीर्तिताः ।...क्षमस्वेत्यर्थनैवैका निष्कृति र्निरुपद्रवा ॥
summary: This appendix outlines the code of conduct for devotees in a Hindu temple, drawing from the Vaikhānasa texts, specifically Chapters 20 and 36 of Bhṛgu's 'Prakīrṇādhikāra'. It provides a detailed list of prescriptions and prohibitions covering attire, physical actions, mental state, and social interactions within the temple premises. The rules, which apply to both men and women, aim to preserve the temple's sanctity and ensure that worship is performed with the utmost reverence and purity of mind and body. The appendix concludes with a consolidated list of twenty-two specific offenses to be avoided.
purpose: The purpose of this appendix is to educate devotees on the proper 'temple-culture' as prescribed by the Vaikhānasa tradition. It aims to establish a standard code of conduct that maintains the sacred atmosphere of the temple, focusing on the devotee's reverence, purity, and mindful behavior to ensure a meaningful and spiritually correct visit to the shrine.
key_information: **Source**: The rules are derived from the Vaikhānasa texts, specifically Bhṛgu's *Prakīrṇādhikāra* (Chapters 20 and 36).
**Prohibitions on Entry**: Do not enter with footwear, in a vehicle, empty-handed, while unclean, or while sick/distressed.
**Proper Attire**: Wear clean, traditional, unstitched garments (dhoti, uttarīya). Prohibits stitched clothes, headgear, and weapons. The sacred cord must be worn correctly.
**Prohibited Actions**: Do not eat, sleep, stretch legs towards the deity, sit with one's back to the deity, expel flatulence, cry, quarrel, gossip, or engage in worldly discussions.
**Proper Actions**: Circumambulate the shrine before entering, prostrate, bring an offering, and maintain focus on the deity through meditation.

**Mental and Social Conduct**: Maintain a pure and steady mind. Do not lie, speak harshly, praise or condemn others (including oneself), or bow to any other person within the temple. Humility and reverence are paramount.
**Respect for Ritual Timing**: Devotees must respect the temple's schedule and not demand access to the deity when the sanctum is screened off or closed.
**List of Offenses**: A summary list of 22 specific offensive acts is provided at the end for clarity.
**Remedy for Offenses**: For any offenses committed inadvertently, one should ask for forgiveness (kṣamā-yācanā).

tables_and_data.description: A consolidated list of twenty-two acts regarded as offensive in a temple is presented in point 27 of the appendix.
tables_and_data.data_summary: The list enumerates specific prohibitions, including: (1) Using vehicles or footwear; (2) Ignoring ceremonies; (3) Improper obeisance; (4) Prostrating while unclean; (5) Stretching legs towards the deity; (6) Sleeping; (7) Eating; (8) Gossiping; (9) Loud talk/quarreling; (10) Exercising authority (punishment/favour); (11) Obscene talk; (12) Expelling flatulence; (13) Covering with blankets; (14) Praising/condemning others; (15) Honouring influential people; (16) Eating non-prasāda food; (17) Not offering seasonal produce; (18) Misusing leftover offerings; (19) Turning one's back to the deity; (20) Improper greetings; (21) Praising oneself; (22) Criticizing the deity.

references_to_chapters: The appendix explicitly states that its content is based on excerpts from Bhṛgu's Prakīrṇādhikāra, Chapters 20 and 36.
Numerous parenthetical citations throughout the text refer to specific chapters and verse numbers from this source, such as (36,1), (20, 113), (27,280), (36, 312-313), etc.
